name: IntentRedirectionSpec
source_title: IntentRedirection.crysl — requested canonical CrySL source could not be retrieved
protocol: receiveOuterIntent -> extractNestedIntent -> (resolveTarget && sameApplicationId && targetInAllowlist) -> launch; report shape: extractNestedIntent -> launch where validation is not evidenced
important_note: android.content.IntentRedirection is a nominal, unverified CrySL-style target included to meet the required XSpec naming convention; it is not evidence of an Android SDK runtime class. The requested canonical raw CrySL URL was reported as fetched but unavailable (HTTP 404), so this context reconstructs the reported Android intent-redirection detector shape rather than establishing a verified CrySL rule.

events.name: receive_outer_intent
events.condition: Observation: code accesses an Activity-delivered Intent or the nested-intent extra. Predicate satisfaction: the outer Intent is externally reachable or attacker-influenced; this requires version-matched manifest, permission, caller, and routing evidence.

events.name: extract_nested_intent
events.condition: Observation: a Parcelable Intent is read from an extra. Predicate satisfaction: the extracted value is data/control-flow derived from an attacker-influenced outer Intent and is the value that reaches the launch sink.

events.name: resolve_and_validate_target
events.condition: Observation: target resolution, package comparison, allowlist comparison, or sanitizer construction appears. Predicate satisfaction: the exact nested Intent passed to the sink is rejected unless its resolved target and relevant mutable properties satisfy the application's security policy; unrelated or unconnected checks do not satisfy this predicate.

events.name: launch_nested_intent
events.condition: Observation: a component-launch API or local wrapper is called. Predicate satisfaction: the argument reaching that sink is the extracted nested Intent; observing a launch call alone does not establish intent redirection or exploitability.

forbidden_inferences_without_evidence: Do not infer that android.content.IntentRedirection is a real Android SDK class; its nominal type is unverified because the canonical CrySL source was unavailable.
Do not infer exploitability merely from nested-Intent extraction and a launch call.
Do not infer that MainActivity was exported, permissionless, or reachable by an arbitrary third-party app without inspecting the version-matched manifest and runtime entry conditions.
Do not infer that every nested-Intent launch is unsafe; safety depends on provenance and complete validation or sanitization before launch.
Do not infer that a package-name check alone is sufficient for every policy; component targeting and URI-grant flags can also be relevant.
Do not infer that the detector recognizes all equivalent validation helpers, launch sinks, Kotlin extensions, reflection, or framework-mediated launches.
Do not infer a runtime compromise, affected-device population, or impact beyond the normalized advisory record without version-matched reproduction evidence.
semantic_scope: The rule concept concerns Android intent redirection: an application component receives an outer Intent, extracts a nested Intent from extras, and launches that nested Intent. The representative finding concerns im.vector.app.features.MainActivity.handleAppStarted in Element Android tag v1.6.10, identifies EXTRA_NEXT_INTENT as the source, and reports launch through startIntentAndFinish without the application-ID and activity-allowlist validation stated to be present in the fix.

detector_semantics.claim: The normalized finding claims that handleAppStarted reads a nested Intent from EXTRA_NEXT_INTENT on an externally reachable Intent and starts it without recognized target validation; the selected v1.6.10 source is stated to predate the application-ID and activity-allowlist check introduced by the fix.
predicates: A delivered outer Intent is modeled as externally reachable or attacker-influenced.
A nested Intent is obtained from the EXTRA_NEXT_INTENT extra.
The nested Intent flows to an activity-launch operation, directly or through startIntentAndFinish.
No recognized target-validation predicate protects that launch on the reported path.
The analyzed source corresponds to the vulnerable version line represented by tag v1.6.10.
limitations: The actual IntentRedirection.crysl source and its exact CrySL EVENTS, ORDER, CONSTRAINTS, and predicates could not be verified.
The normalized advisory record is not a runtime trace, exploit reproduction, manifest analysis, or proof that an untrusted caller can reach the path in a particular build.
The record does not disclose the detector's precise data-flow, call-graph, aliasing, nullability, reflection, lifecycle, or validation-recognition behavior.

Historical v1.6.10 source is reported to extract the nested Intent and call a wrapper, while v1.6.12 is reported to resolve the activity and require the resolved package to equal buildMeta.applicationId and the class name to be in an explicit allowlist.

documented_behavior: Android documents intent redirection as an attacker partly or fully controlling an Intent that a vulnerable app uses to launch another component; a nested Intent in extras is a common source.
Android's documented mitigation is to validate the redirected target, including expected package and class, or sanitize the Intent before launching it.
preconditions: An outer Intent must be delivered to the application component.
A nested Intent must be extracted from extras or reconstructed from attacker-influenced data.
A component-launch operation must be reached with that nested Intent.

For the reported Element Android case, the relevant historical source is tag v1.6.10; v1.6.12 is reported to resolve the activity and require both application-ID equality and an explicit activity allowlist.
unknowns: Whether the unavailable intended CrySL rule models only startActivity or also startService, bindService, pending-intent dispatch, and other component launches.
Whether the intended rule requires a specific extra key such as EXTRA_NEXT_INTENT or treats any nested-Intent extra as a source.
Whether validation is limited to package and class allowlisting or also includes action, data URI, categories, flags, permissions, exported state, and URI-grant handling.
Whether android.content.IntentRedirection is a project-defined pseudo-type, a detector-internal nominal API type, or an intended source declaration absent from the public corpus.

security_semantics.detector_claim: A potentially attacker-supplied nested Intent reaches a launch sink without a recognized target-validation step.
security_semantics.runtime_claim: A vulnerability exists only if an untrusted party can cause the component to receive a chosen or sufficiently controlled nested Intent, the application launches it on the relevant path, and Android and component configuration permit a security-relevant result.

source_level: Retrieve the exact IntentRedirection.crysl file, including its SPEC declaration, EVENTS, ORDER, CONSTRAINTS, and predicate definitions.
Inspect the exact application source at the selected tag and resolve helpers such as startIntentAndFinish.
Inspect the version-matched AndroidManifest.xml or merged manifest, intent filters, exported attributes, and component permissions for MainActivity.
Confirm source-to-artifact version mapping rather than relying solely on a repository tag or advisory normalization.
runtime: Demonstrate that an untrusted application or other untrusted origin can deliver the required outer Intent under the tested installation configuration.
Demonstrate that EXTRA_NEXT_INTENT accepts a nested Intent controlled by that origin.
Demonstrate that the same nested Intent reaches the launch operation and resolves to a security-relevant target.
Record Android version, target SDK, installed application ID, component-export configuration, launch result, and applicable system hardening behavior.
compatibility: Test the affected Element Android range identified by CVE-2024-26131, reported as versions 1.4.3 through 1.6.10, with 1.6.12 reported as fixed.

Account for Android-version behavior, including documented default intent-redirection hardening in Android 16 and StrictMode detection conditions for certain nested-Intent unparcel-and-launch patterns on apps targeting Android 12 or later.
Verify build flavors and application IDs, because the reported fix compares the resolved package with buildMeta.applicationId.

known_false_positive_shapes: The reported activity is not externally reachable in the analyzed artifact because it is unexported, protected by a non-bypassable permission, or lacks a reachable intent route.
The EXTRA_NEXT_INTENT value is always internally constructed on feasible paths despite a coarse attacker-source model.
Complete validation or sanitization occurs in a helper, superclass, lifecycle callback, library wrapper, or interprocedural path that the detector does not recognize.
The launch wrapper receives null or a separately constructed safe Intent rather than the extracted nested Intent.
The nested Intent can resolve only to an intended public component and cannot convey security-relevant URI grants, extras, actions, or flags in the deployed configuration.
The scanned revision, flavor, fork, or generated artifact differs from tag v1.6.10.
Platform-level protections prevent observed redirection behavior on a tested device, without proving the source-level pattern safe on all supported platforms.
unknowns: What exact fully qualified type is declared by the intended IntentRedirection.crysl rule, if such a rule exists; android.content.IntentRedirection is included only as the required nominal CrySL-style target and remains unverified.
The canonical CrySL source content, including exact event names, accepted method signatures, order expression, constraints, and error condition.
Whether the canonical source was moved, renamed, generated, private, or never present in the referenced CROSSINGTUD repository path.
The exact detector implementation behind IntentRedirectionSpec and whether the normalized finding is generated from CrySL, a separate Android security rule, or a hybrid rule.
The version-matched merged-manifest reachability and permission configuration for im.vector.app.features.MainActivity.
Whether a concrete v1.6.10 build permits a third-party app to supply the required nested Intent on the tested Android version and deployment configuration.

source_verification.note: Accepted as unverifiable without further attempts: the proposed source was checked directly and could not be retrieved.

detector_examples.message: External finding (CVE-2024-26131): handleAppStarted reads an Intent from the EXTRA_NEXT_INTENT extra of an externally reachable Intent and starts it without validating its target. The selected version lacks the application-id and activity allowlist check introduced by the fix. Source tag: v1.6.10. This is a normalized advisory record, not a runtime log.
